about.mcskincreator.what: MC Skin Creator builds a skin out of layers: an element picked from the library sits on top of the last one, and the 64 by 64 sheet is rebuilt on every change.
about.mcskincreator.local_only: What you build stays on your machine until you apply it. Applying sends it to your Minecraft account, puts it on you here straight away, and everyone else sees it once Minecraft hands it out — the editor never does that on its own.
about.mcskincreator.author: Made by %s
beta.mcskincreator.body: The editor is being written. The drawing tools and the per-element colours are not here yet.
legal.mcskincreator.body: Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Studios. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mojang Studios or Microsoft.
credits.mcskincreator.body: The interface is MC Skin Creator's. The elements come from the site's catalogue, and each work that this stack draws on is credited below.
provenance.mcskincreator.body: %s (%s): where this element was cut from.
import.mcskincreator.body: Importing a skin already made will lay it down as a single layer that the colour settings can still work on.
import.mcskincreator.not_yet: Reading a file is not written yet. The button stays here to say where it will land.
apply.mcskincreator.what: This replaces the skin on your Minecraft account with the one you have built. It is the same change the official launcher makes: everyone sees it, on every server, and it stays after you close the game.
apply.mcskincreator.model: The classic or slim model chosen in the editor goes up with the skin, so the arms are the width you drew them for.
apply.mcskincreator.propagation: You will see the new skin on yourself straight away — the mod puts it on this client the moment Minecraft accepts it. Other players will not: Minecraft's profile servers take tens of seconds, sometimes longer, to hand it out. Applying again does not speed that up; it only gets you rate-limited.
export.mcskincreator.file_detail: Writes the 64 by 64 sheet into the game's mcskincreator folder.
